significance: The principal temple of the Gowda Saraswat Brahmins of Cochin, consecrated in 1599 by Swami Sudhindra Thirtha for a Venkateshwara image brought from Goa by families fleeing Portuguese persecution. The Portuguese destroyed it in 1662 and it was rebuilt the following year under Dutch rule; after further trouble in 1791 the image was kept at Alappuzha until it was brought back in 1853.
story: The image is held to be swayambhu, said to have been shaped by Vishvakarma himself through a sculptor working for the Vijayanagara king Saluva Narasimha Deva Raya.
